reason: The single cited study (E1) directly supports all key premises: it reports Hf-rich precipitate formation at interfaces/B2 phase, hindrance of grain-boundary sliding and dislocation motion, improved high-temperature strength/ductility peaking near 0.5 at% Hf, and nearly unchanged room-temperature properties. Density is not explicitly mentioned in the cited passage, but the premise of negligible density increase is a minor overstatement relative to the provided evidence.
premises: Hf addition (~0.5 at%) to a dual-phase RHEA forms fine Hf-rich precipitates at interfaces and within the B2 phase.
These precipitates hinder grain-boundary sliding and dislocation motion during high-temperature deformation.
This leads to improved high-temperature strength and ductility.
Room-temperature mechanical properties remain almost unchanged.
